message.content: {"answer": "D", "option_text": "Progressive atelectasis in the right lower lobe suggesting foreign body obstruction.", "reason": "The provided images are axial and coronal CT scans (not chest X-rays), showing a hyperdense, calcified structure (measuring ~425 HU) within the right lower lobe bronchus. This high-density object is consistent with an aspirated foreign body (e.g., tooth or bone) causing endobronchial obstruction. The resulting downstream lung collapse represents progressive atelectasis. Options A, C, E, and F are inconsistent with the focal obstructive pathology seen. Option B (mucous plugging) is less likely given the extreme density of the obstructing material."}
